additional_info.subject: Note from TS
additional_info.body: It seems EV is not upscaling, yes we start at a low current of 100A but reach 250A in minutes, but the EV doesn't react to our change and since it doesn't react to our change, the charger downscales and never ramps up because the EV is not upscaling. Indeed strange that the Current Max is changing from 100A->250A->100A->250A->600A

additional_info.subject: ID0479872-DC/Si-D/SE-[ ] Siemens problems with DAF NGD electric CRM:02565000816
additional_info.body:
Hi Rasmus, good morning.
Thanks again for your feedback.
From my point of view, I always try to find if there is any constraints in our system before pushing to the truck manufacturer.
I will share with you the logs from our session for better understanding. When we start the charging process, the Sicharge D allocates 282kW for this truck:
According to the ParameterDiscovery:
This is the part where the vehicle doesn't ask for more current at:
09:00:33
I also found it strange that it took so long to heat up the system, the truck definitely doesn't ask for more than ~110A at
09:12:35
Eventually after 30mins we can see that the cable limitation is no longer present:
But the truck is never ramping up the current at any point in time after it reaches this ~100A.
We will investigate if this limitation is due to the fact that the EV is not asking for more than 100A and as such, the heating for the cable is never necessary, and with the normal charging operation, it heats up naturally and eventually can charge the maximum current.
I will keep you updated with the latest findings, and if you find a timeslot for testing let me know. If possible we would also like to have the Scania to completely prove that it's an incompatibility solely with DAF and not a general issue.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0479872-DC/Si-D/SE-[ ] Siemens problems with DAF NGD electric CRM:02565000816
additional_info.body:
Hello Rasmus,
Thanks for this particular message one @ 17 and two @ 18.
I did an analysis from the 18th on a wrong session. But my analysis stays true, this is not a problem with the trucks, but a constraint regarding the temperature.
According to the logic of the pump, it only gets activated, bearing in mind that we are below 0ºC, when the EV request for more than 100A. In this case, it really takes ~10mins to heat up and be able to charge up to maximum.
If you do not own the charger, then my recommendation is, in the future, use the Sicharge 400 with air cooled cables, depending on the configuration, these ones go up to 500A boost mode and then 375A, without any logic of cooling/heating.
If the charging gets limited to 400A most likely it's the 250A/400A cable.
Please let me know your feedback, in general, there is no problem with the system, this is how it was designed.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0479872-DC/Si-D/SE-[ ] Siemens problems with DAF NGD electric CRM:02565000816
additional_info.body:
Thanks for the information Francisco, but I think you have wrong (can't promise it, but I hope).
If it is as you describe, we need to reclaim this charger and change that one to another brand (it is our own charger).
We can in this case not buy any more of them as well (we have a offer now on 2 more).
It take to long time to charge a truck if we need to wait the hole time that the charger heats up before it can deliver the requested power.
We have asked many questions before we bought this charger. And have been promised that it can deliver >500A cont.
We even replaced a Sicharge 400 with normal cables due to to low Amps (tested that first). Every graph we have got and all specification in data sheet shows that Sicharge 400 with liquid cold cables can provide 600A up to a certain temperature (not only above a certain temp).
If this is the case we need to get that information to PACCAR and all DAF Dealers as fast as possible. So no more of them being delivered to places that can have below 0ºC in temperatures.
Extra important with DAF because them only can charge with 500A the first 10min so it's the slowest charging speed on the market already, without getting lower because the chargers bad logic "too have a cooling system that not working when it not need to work" (when you not need to cool the cables with liquid).
We have received support from the Swedish Transport Authority for this charger, where the requirements are that it must be able to deliver 500A continuously (at least 45 minutes and an average of 60 minutes).

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0479872-DC/Si-D/SE-[ ] Siemens problems with DAF NGD electric CRM:02565000816
additional_info.body:
Dear Francisco,
My name is Richard Krieckaart and I am an e-mobility specialist within PACCAR Power Solutions, a subsidiary within PACCAR Parts Europe and DAF Trucks, located in Eindhoven, The Netherlands. I am asked to assist in finding a resolution for the reported issue by LIR Teknik, where, as I understood so far, multiple charging sessions did not go well with a DAF vehicle on their Siemens 400kW Sicharge D charger with liquid cooled cables.
I received the mailing related to the service ticket with reference number ID0479872 from Rasmus Lindé. What I understand from this mailing is that there are potentially 3 charging sessions that showed the same issue, where the charger only provided 50% of the (vehicle) maximum power (160kW/250A) for 10 minutes. After these 10 minutes, continuous charging with 260 kW/400A is running as expected.
Can you share the data log files of the charging sessions of the 17
th
and 18
th
Feb, so that we can analyze them, in order to find and determine the root cause of the behavior that we see?
We are also trying to retrieve all the data from the vehicle to compare everything and approach this case both from the vehicle and charger side. The MAC address of the vehicle should be 0C:73:EB:A6:06:06
Thank you in advance for your support.
Met vriendelijke groet, Kind regards,
Richard Krieckaart
Specialist e-Mobility Solutions
|
PACCAR
Power Solutions
| DAF Trucks N.V. |
M: +31 (0) 6 12 77 48 99 |
